landing.archSub: Three Questions Every Urban Resident Faces
landing.q1Title: 1. What am I breathing right now?
landing.q1Desc: Clear real-time US AQI and European AQI metrics grounded in continuous Open-Meteo & Copernicus atmospheric dispersion telemetry.
landing.q2Title: 2. What should I do differently today?
landing.q2Desc: Contextual daily plans tailored for students, working professionals, homemakers, and caregivers. Smarter commute hours, evidence-based ventilation guidance, and mask advice.
landing.q3Title: 3. Can my choices make a difference?
landing.q3Desc: Direct low-emission transit comparisons showing exact tailpipe grams of CO2 and PM2.5 prevented using verified ARAI & DEFRA vehicle factors.
landing.sampleWhyText: Early morning temperature inversions compress fine particulates (PM2.5) near ground level, tripling inhalation load during strenuous breathing.
landing.sampleAction1: Switch to indoor stationary cardio or yoga today.
landing.sampleAction2: Check current hourly air-quality readings before planning outdoor errands. Avoid periods of elevated pollution.

protocols.maskSevereDesc: Ambient particulate levels are elevated. High-efficiency respiratory protection (N95/FFP2) is recommended during outdoor transit.
protocols.maskElevatedDesc: Individuals with asthma or cardiovascular conditions should limit prolonged outdoor exertion.
protocols.maskNormalDesc: Ambient particulate concentrations are within standard healthy exposure limits.
protocols.ventSevereDesc: Elevated ambient particulate density. Keep windows sealed and operate indoor filtration when available.
protocols.ventElevatedDesc: Solar heating generally enhances atmospheric boundary layer mixing in the afternoon (12:00–16:00), making it the preferred window for brief ventilation.
protocols.ventNormalDesc: Ambient air quality permits natural indoor ventilation throughout the day.

pollutantMatrix.title: Atmospheric Pollutant Concentration Matrix
pollutantMatrix.subtitle: Current surface readings displayed with WHO 2021 Air Quality Guidelines for contextual reference (health-based benchmarks defined on a 99th-percentile basis, permitting ~3–4 exceedance days annually, not legal ceilings). Direct ratios are calculated only when measurement averaging periods match WHO reference windows.
pollutantMatrix.pm25Desc: Deep alveolar penetration & systemic vascular uptake.
pollutantMatrix.pm10Desc: Upper bronchial irritation and thoracic airway loading.
pollutantMatrix.no2Desc: Thermal combustion marker; induces airway hyperresponsiveness.
pollutantMatrix.o3Desc: Photochemical oxidant; reduces pulmonary forced vital capacity.
pollutantMatrix.so2Desc: Fossil fuel combustion byproduct; provokes acute bronchospasm.
pollutantMatrix.coDesc: Forms carboxyhemoglobin, impeding cellular oxygen transport.

methodology.label: Methodological Transparency:
methodology.text: Real-time and forecasted indices are synthesized using standard US EPA and European Environmental Agency (EEA) transfer functions. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) NAQI sub-indices are derived using Indian national 24-hour breakpoints when continuous monitoring station feeds are linked.

dashboard.advisoryHigh: High particulate matter suspension. Avoid early morning jogging or vigorous outdoor workouts. Check current hourly AQI before airing rooms; keep windows sealed during peak smog intervals. Note: indoor air quality is unmonitored.
dashboard.advisoryModerate: Particulate density is moderate. Keep indoor spaces clean with damp mopping and opt for public transit or carpooling.
dashboard.advisoryLow: Atmospheric dispersion is healthy. Favorable ambient conditions for outdoor physical exercise and natural ventilation.

dashboard.askVentilate: When is the best time to ventilate my home today?

indoor.title: Indoor Air Guardian
indoor.subtitle: Science-backed indoor air quality protocol for winter smog periods. (Note: Indoor air is unmonitored; metrics reflect outdoor ambient data).
indoor.card1Summary: Before opening windows, check current hourly outdoor AQI readings. Avoid ventilating during cold morning inversion hours when ground-level exhaust stagnates.
indoor.card1Step1: Ventilate only if verified hourly outdoor AQI confirms acceptable ambient conditions; never assume midday is automatically safe.
indoor.card1Step2: If outdoor readings are favorable, create brief cross-ventilation for 10-15 minutes, then latch windows securely.
indoor.card1Step3: Use draft-stopper seals or rolled towels beneath exterior doors facing corridors to limit particulate infiltration.
indoor.card1Why: Thermal temperature inversion occurs when cold surface air is trapped beneath warmer air aloft, compressing particulate matter close to breathing height.
indoor.card2Summary: High-heat oil frying, deep tempering, and unvented gas stoves can cause indoor PM2.5 spikes up to 400 µg/m³ within 15 minutes.
indoor.card2Step1: Turn on kitchen chimney/exhaust fan at least 60 seconds BEFORE igniting stove burners.
indoor.card2Step2: Keep the kitchen door closed from living rooms and bedrooms while cooking.
indoor.card2Step3: Cover pans during boiling and shallow frying to prevent aerosolized lipid droplets from escaping into room air.
indoor.card2Step4: Never rely on chemical aerosol room fresheners or citrus sprays—they react with ozone to form formaldehyde and secondary particulates.
indoor.card2Why: Incomplete LPG combustion emits nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and carbon monoxide, while vaporized cooking oils condense into ultrafine respirable aerosol particles.
indoor.card3Summary: Traditional dry broom sweeping and feather dusters fling settled heavy and fine particulates back into breathing suspension.
indoor.card3Step1: Strictly switch to damp microfiber mopping and microfiber electrostatic cloths.
indoor.card3Step2: Vacuum exclusively with sealed HEPA-grade exhaust filters; ordinary bag vacuums blow fine particles right back into the room.
indoor.card3Step3: Wash bed linens and curtains in warm water (60°C) bi-weekly to neutralize dust-mite allergens and trapped exterior soot.
indoor.card3Why: Mechanical dry sweeping resuspends PM10 and PM2.5 for up to 2 to 4 hours in stagnant indoor air.
indoor.card4Summary: Understand true particulate filtration capabilities versus common marketing myths.
indoor.card4Step1: True HEPA H13 filters capture 99.97% of particles down to 0.3 microns. Verify genuine H13 certification.
indoor.card4Step2: Place air purifiers centrally away from walls and at least 3 feet off the floor for optimal laminar airflow circulation.
indoor.card4Step3: Myth check: Indoor plants (snake plant, spider plant) have ZERO measurable effect on clearing high-concentration particulate smog (PM2.5). They absorb trace VOCs under high laboratory conditions but cannot replace mechanical filtration.
indoor.card4Step4: Clean or vacuum pre-filters every 2 weeks to extend true HEPA lifespan and reduce motor resistance.
indoor.cadrGuideDesc: Never buy an air purifier based on room square footage claims alone. Match Clean Air Delivery Rate (CADR) to achieve 4 to 5 complete air changes per hour (ACH).
